content.title: Who's in 2026 NHL playoffs? Latest bracket, standings as four teams clinch
content.text: April 11, 2026Updated April 12, 2026, 10:40 a.m. ETThe NHL's busy 15-game schedule on Saturday, April 11 provided more clarity in the playoff race.The Boston Bruins and Ottawa Senators clinched wild-card berths (swapping positions in the process). The Edmonton Oilers and Vegas Golden Knights also joined the nine teams that made the postseason earlier. The idle Anaheim Ducks didn't get the right combination to clinch on SaturdayThe Pacific Division lead changed hands with the Oilers losing and Golden Knights passing them with a 3-2 overtime win against the Colorado Avalanche. The second wild-card seed in the Western Conference stayed the same as both the Los Angeles Kings and Nashville Predators both won. The Kings hold a one-point lead and are three points back of the Utah Mammoth, the first wild card.The Tampa Bay Lightning won and moved into second place in the Atlantic Division as the Montreal Canadiens lost.Here's what to know about the NHL standings, including the latest playoff bracket, Saturday's clinching scenarios and the tiebreaker procedures for the 2025-26 season: Golden Knights beat Avalanche: What it meansVegas' 3-2 overtime win not only clinches a playoff spot, but the Golden Knights pass the Oilers for the Pacific Division lead. The game had a scary moment when Avalanche coach Jared Bednar was hit by a puck in the face on the bench and had to leave the game. He didn't return but was fully alert and was going to the hospital for a CT scan. Golden Knights, Avalanche tied after twoIt's 2-2. The Golden Knights will need to win to move into the Pacific Division lead. Edmonton has more regulation wins, the first tiebreaker. Blue Jackets beat Canadiens: What it meansColumbus wins 5-2. The Blue Jackets remain two points behind the Flyers for the third seed in the Metropolitan Division, the only seed the teams can claim. Both have two games left and Columbus holds the first tiebreaker. The Canadiens' loss drops them to third place in the Atlantic behind Tampa Bay. If that holds up, the Lightning would have home-ice advantage in the first round. Both of those teams could still pass Buffalo for the Atlantic Division title. All three have two games left. Flyers beat Jets: What it meansThe Flyers' 7-1 rout keeps them in third place in the Metropolitan Division. The Jets' loss clinches a playoff berth for the Oilers. Winnipeg remains alive in the wild-card race in the West, but barely. It must win its final three games and hope for help or the Jets will join the Rangers as Presidents' Trophy winners to miss the playoffs the following season. Golden Knights-Avalanche underwayIf Vegas wins, it will pass Edmonton and move into the Pacific Division lead. The score is tied 1-1 after one period. Predators beat Wild: What it meansThe Predators' 2-1 win keeps them one point behind the Kings in the battle for the second wild card. The Minnesota loss makes it impossible for it to catch Dallas for second place in the Central. The Wild will start on the road against the Stars, who shut out the Rangers on Saturday. The Blues and Kraken were also officially eliminated on Saturday. Senators, Bruins clinch; Red Wings eliminatedThe Red Wings went ahead 3-2 in the third period, but the Devils scored three consecutive goals for a 5-3 victory. That clinches playoff berths for the Bruins and Senators, who needed a Detroit loss. The Red Wings are eliminated from playoff contention and their 10-season drought is the NHL's longest after the Sabres ended their 14-year absence. Key 7 p.m. NHL gamesColumbus at Montreal and Philadelphia at Winnipeg. The Blue Jackets would move into third place in the Metropolitan if they win and the Flyers lose in regulation. A Canadiens regulation loss would drop them to third in the Atlantic. If the Jets do anything but beat the Flyers in regulation, the Oilers clinch a playoff berth. Columbus and Philadelphia have taken early leads. Kings beat Oilers: What it meansLos Angeles' 1-0 win will keep it ahead of the Predators, who are leading their game after two periods. The Kings have fewer regulation wins, so they must finish in front of Nashville in points. The Kings also pulled within two points of the third place Ducks in the Pacific Division.The game was the Kings' home finale and captain Anze Kopitar addressed the fans afterward. The Kings all-time leading scorer is retiring after this season.The Oilers' loss means the Golden Knights could pass them for the Pacific Division lead if they beat the Avalanche later Saturday. Edmonton could still clinch a playoff berth on Saturday if the Jets don't beat the Flyers in regulation. Capitals beat Penguins: What it meansWashington's 6-3 win keeps its playoff hopes alive. It is one point behind the third-place Flyers in the race for third in the Metropolitan Division. Alex Ovechkin scored his 929th career goal, an empty-netter, in what could be his final game in Pittsburgh.The game meant nothing for the Penguins, who are locked into second place in the Metropolitan. They rested players, citing injuries, including Sidney Crosby, Evgeni Malkin, Kris Letang and Erik Karlsson. Other key 5 p.m. ET NHL gamesThe Predators, facing the Wild, can move into the second wild card with a win and a Kings loss. Minnesota needs to win to have a shot at home-ice advantage. But Dallas will clinch second in the Central with a win against the Rangers, regardless of what the Wild do. Red Wings facing DevilsThis game is important to the Red Wings, Senators and Bruins. If the Red Wings lose, the Senators clinch. If Detroit loses in regulation, Boston clinches. If that happens, then the Red Wings' playoff drought extends to 10 seasons. Oilers facing KingsEdmonton can build on its Pacific Division lead with a win and can clinch a playoff berth by picking up one point. Los Angeles can build on its lead in the race for the second wild card with a win. The Kings are up 1-0 after one period. Senators beat Islanders: What it meansThe Senators win 3-0 and move into the first wild card in the East on a tiebreaker. Boston drops to the second wild card. Ottawa needs a Red Wings loss in order to clinch on Saturday. If Detroit loses in regulation, the Bruins also clinch. The Islanders fail to gain ground in the race for third in Metropolitan and remain one point behind the Flyers and out of the playoffs.The Senators lost captain Brady Tkachuk after a collision near the bench in the second period. He skated one shift in the third period, then left the game. Senators coach Travis Green said after the game that Tkachuk "just wasn't feeling well." Capitals-Penguins underwayNo real playoff implications here, though the Capitals will stay alive with a win. The Penguins are resting many veterans, citing injuries. Sidney Crosby is one of those who's day-to-day so no 100th career meeting of the Penguins star and Capitals star Alex Ovechkin. Lightning beat Bruins: What it means?The Lightning rallied past the Bruins for a 2-1 regulation win as Emil Lilleberg broke a tie with 1:35 left. Tampa Bay ties Montreal for second in the Atlantic with 104 points, though the Canadiens play later on Saturday. Boston fails to clinch outright, but the Bruins can back their way in if the Red Wings lose in regulation and the Islanders or Flyers also lose in regulation. New York trails Ottawa 1-0 in the third period. Bruins, Senators take leadsThe Bruins and Senators, who can clinch playoff berths on Saturday, have scored first in their games. Ottawa's Randy Greig has a short-handed goal against the Islanders. Boston's Morgan Geekie scored a breakaway goal against the Lightning. The Bruins clinch with a win, the Senators with a win and a Red Wings loss. Brady Tkachuk, Anders Lee fight off opening faceoffThe Senators and Islanders captains dropped the gloves right off the opening faceoff on Saturday. They did the same in the teams' last meeting on March 19. An Islanders regulation win on Saturday would pull the team within one point of the Senators for the second wild card, though New York could move into third in the Metropolitan if the Philadelphia Flyers lose. No Sidney Crosby-Alex Ovechkin matchup todayWashington's Alex Ovechkin and Pittsburgh's Sidney Crosby were supposed to have their 100th career meeting today, but it won't happen. Crosby is day-to-day with a lower-body injury. Evgeni Malkin, Bryan Rust, Erik Karlsson and Kris Letang are among others sitting out because of injuries, the team said.Who's in the 2026 NHL playoffs?Eastern Conference: Carolina, Buffalo, Montreal, Tampa Bay, Pittsburgh, Ottawa, BostonWestern Conference: Colorado, Dallas, Minnesota, Utah, Edmonton, VegasWho could clinch an NHL playoff berth today?The Boston Bruins will clinch a playoff berth if they beat the Lightning. They'd also clinch if they get one point, the Red Wings lose and the Senators and/or Flyers lose. A third option: The Red Wings lose in regulation and the Islanders or Flyers lose. Update: The Bruins lost, but losses by the Islanders and Red Wings clinched a berth for Boston.The Ottawa Senators will clinch a playoff berth if they beat the Islanders and the Red Wings lose. Update: Both happened and the Senators are in.The Edmonton Oilers will clinch a playoff berth if they get at least one point against the Kings. They also clinch if the Jets fail to win in regulation. Update: The Oilers lost but so did the Jets, so they clinch.The Vegas Golden Knights will clinch a playoff berth if they beat the Avalanche. They'd also clinch if they get one point and the Jets and Predators lose. Third option: The Sharks lose and the Jets and Predators lose in regulation. Update: The Golden Knights clinched with an overtime victory.The idle Anaheim Ducks will clinch a playoff berth if the Sharks lose and the Jets and Predators lose in regulation.
